newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS SEEN RETREATING ON CONSOLIDATION.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS SEEN RETREATING ON CONSOLIDATION.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to edge lower on Friday on continued consolidation from Thursday afternoon, which should absorb some of the selling pressure before 750, brokers said.
"Consolidation is expected to stay for another day before the market heads on another march," said Park Joo-chang of Daewoo Securities.
The composite stock index closed Thursday down 0.30 points to 745.35.
Brokers said some investors may choose to step aside, searching for fresh market leaders to take the index above 750.
"General sentiment isn't bad," said a broker at Dongwon Securities. "The market just needs time to consolidate."
Shares of Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store are expected to stay firm for another day on the news that emergency funds had been supplied to the two troubled firms.
"Dainong shares will continue to be strong today because they had fallen quite a lot previously," said Park of Daewoo.
Brokers said any developments with the troubled Kia Group would be watched closely. -- JEAN YOON (822) 727 5643
